sanitization: No account IDs, cluster names, endpoints, database names, usernames, credentials, tokens, query text, or raw collector logs are recorded.

evidence.transport: Both database clients and receivers used certificate-verifying TLS; workload clients negotiated TLS 1.3.
evidence.workload: Each engine completed 90 controlled queries across the 10-second query-sample and 60-second top-query intervals.
evidence.lifecycle: The guarded Helm 4 apply, scoped live validation, state-backed rollback, isolated release uninstall, namespace UID-checked deletion, and zero-residue checks passed.
evidence.regression_suite: 70 pytest tests passed, 3 skipped; 15 Bats tests passed; ShellCheck, Python compilation, and diff checks passed.

limitations: The DBMon product UI, query details, explain plans, dependencies, metadata, alerts, APM correlation, and AI query assistance were not directly verified.
MariaDB explain plans are not supported by the pinned receiver.
SQL Server, Oracle Database, and provider-paired PostgreSQL were not part of this run.
runs.cleanup: All run-scoped Kubernetes resources, Helm state, local rendered artifacts, port-forwards, and containers were removed; the pre-existing collector release was unchanged.

targets: Microsoft SQL Server 2022 CU25 Developer self-hosted

evidence.isolation: All database fixtures, jobs, and the singleton cluster receiver ran in a dedicated namespace on one temporary tainted and node-selected On-Demand worker; the existing shared collector release was not changed.
evidence.transport: PostgreSQL used verify-full TLS 1.3 with the AWS RDS CA; SQL Server used mandatory encrypted TDS over TLS 1.2 with a private CA and hostname verification; Oracle used TCPS over TLS 1.3 with a mounted auto-login wallet.
evidence.least_privilege: PostgreSQL used pg_monitor plus documented statistics grants, with lab-only workload-object reads added to exercise eligible explain plans; SQL Server used the documented 2022 performance-state/database-definition grants and was not sysadmin; Oracle used CREATE SESSION plus the complete 0.155 metric/event view grant set.

positive_exporter_counters.scope: Observed positive absolute DBMon exporter counters after the controlled workloads; these are not claimed as interval deltas.

evidence.lifecycle: Pinned-image config validation, guarded Helm 4 apply, scoped live validation, two automatic failure rollbacks, a committed apply, and an explicit state-backed rollback passed. The explicit rollback restored byte-identical values and manifest without singleton pod-overlap deadlock.
evidence.production_regressions_found_and_fixed: The run corrected SQL Server PEM trust-path handling and grants, completed Oracle view grants, validated secret-backed trust mounts, made singleton rollback quiesce/resume, repeated-rollback lineage, and signal recovery fail closed, added bounded restart-aware current/previous collector-log inspection, distinguished upstream best-effort PostgreSQL per-statement EXPLAIN errors from receiver failure, and changed SignalFlow validation to consume bounded SSE events without waiting for EOF.
evidence.regression_suite: 89 DBMon pytest tests and 15 Kubernetes-helper Bats tests passed. Broader agent/YAML coverage passed 76 tests, 1 skip, and 613 subtests; 11 compatibility/metadata tests and all 166 repository-specific skill-frontmatter checks passed. ShellCheck, Bash syntax checks, Python compilation, validation-registry and compatibility audits, generated-matrix drift check, 7 matrix tests, and diff checks passed.

limitations: The DBMon product UI, query-detail and explain-plan display, dependencies, metadata, and alerts were not directly observed because no authenticated Chrome session was available.
APM trace correlation and licensed AI query assistance were not enabled or verified.
Azure managed variants, AWS RDS MySQL and MariaDB, SQL Server and Oracle managed-service variants, Oracle RAC, Linux service apply, and Windows handoff were not live-tested in this run.
runs.cleanup: The Helm release and namespace, database fixtures and secrets, managed PostgreSQL instance and its dedicated networking, dedicated EKS node group and worker, local credentials/logs, and port-forwards were removed; absence checks passed.
